question: Before the rise of the modern industrial system, Indian exports consisted chiefly of manufactures like________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**cotton and silk fabrics.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Before the rise of the **modern industrial system**, Indian exports consisted chiefly of manufactures like** cotton and silk fabrics.**
 
• Cotton and silk fabrics were the **major exports **from India before the modern industrial system.
 
• India has a rich history of** textile manufacturing, and fabrics **were in high demand in the international market.
 
• The textile industry was the **backbone of the Indian economy **during the pre-industrialization period.
 
• The demand for Indian fabrics was so high that it led to the establishment of the** East India Company in India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electricals:**

 
 
• Electricals were** not **manufactured in India during the pre-industrialization period.
 
• It was only after the British introduced the **electric power system **in India that the manufacturing of electricals began.
 
 
 
• **Chemicals:**
 
 
• Chemicals were **not** a major export from India during the pre-industrialization period.
 
• It was only after the** establishment of the chemical industry** in India that it became a major export.
 
 
 
• **Light Machinery:**
 
 
• Light machinery was **not** manufactured in India during the pre-industrialization period.
 
• It was only after the introduction of the** modern industrial system** in India that the manufacturing of machinery began.
